canonical_name: py_vollib + py_lets_be_rational -- Black-Scholes(-Merton) pricing and Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' implied volatility (vollib)
lineage: Option pricing (Black & Scholes 1973; Merton 1973) and the inverse problem -- implied volatility -- solved to machine precision in two iterations by Peter Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' (2013/2015), a precision-engineering algorithm (rational approximations per branch, careful handling of extreme moneyness). vollib wraps Jaeckel's reference C++ as Python (py_lets_be_rational is the translation).
version: github.com/vollib/py_vollib master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes); py_lets_be_rational from PyPI at run time (recorded)
entry_points: py_vollib.black_scholes.black_scholes(flag, S, K, t, r, sigma); py_vollib.black_scholes.implied_volatility.implied_volatility(price, S, K, t, r, flag)

example.command: python harness: price a grid of options at known sigma, invert, compare
example.output: max |sigma_implied - sigma| ~ 1e-12 (ORACLE: the round trip), including deep OTM cases

upstream_docs: Black & Scholes, The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities, JPE 1973

human_capability_summary.built_to: price European options and, more demandingly, recover the volatility a market price implies, to full double precision, in constant time
human_capability_summary.pressure: markets quoting prices at extreme strikes where naive root-finders lose all digits or fail to converge; latency budgets
human_capability_summary.success_means: the round trip price -> implied vol -> price closes to ~1e-12 across the grid

human_environmental_pressure: numerical ill-conditioning at extreme moneyness, latency
human_failure_condition: the inversion fails or returns a volatility off by percent for deep out-of-the-money options
behavioral_entry_point: push strikes to 5-10 standard deviations and maturities to days; compare against a bisection reference

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run py-vollib-lets-be-rational
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: price European options and, more demandingly, recover the volatility a market price implies, to full double precision, in constant time
